title.narrative: Activity 10: Uganda National Committee Seminar on Gender Mainstreaming in the Prevention of Identity-based Violence

description.narrative: The Uganda National Committee Strategic Planning Meeting and Training Seminar on Gender Mainstreaming in the Prevention of Identity-Based Violence attracted 28 participants and 2 observers during the first week of March 2022, who included UNC members, civil society, government, and academia. The training was conducted in the aftermath of COVID-19-related lockdowns. The Africa Programs Office (APO) followed all government laid out standard operating procedures (SOPs) where all participants, instructors, and staff underwent a covid19 PCR TEST. The goal of the training was to mainstream and strengthen the gender sensitivity and responsiveness of policies and programs implemented toward the prevention of IBV. The training utilized interactive learning led by researchers and practitioners to provide capacity building for different stakeholders while facilitating the application of such knowledge and skills in local contexts. Some of the thematic areas covered include; EWER to gender-based violence in the prevention of IBV; Legal and institutional frameworks for gender mainstreaming IBV; Re-integration of Women and Girls into their communities before, during, and after IBV; Preventing of gender-based violence: policy options and stakeholder roles in the Great Lakes Region, etc. The UNC held a strategic planning meeting on the side whose goal was to develop a strategic framework to implement and increase gender-based responsiveness and sensitivity during the implementation of policies and programs toward the prevention of IBV in Uganda.
